text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima has rejected the consortium's bid for the government's stake in Creditanstalt. A new call for bids will be made soon.
- Metalworkers' wages to rise by two percent. In some other industrial branches wages will rise by 1.7 percent.
- Construction group Rieder/Leitl wants to take over Maculan Holding through the latter's former unit Ebenseer Betonwerke.
- Membership in the European Union has reduced prices for consumer goods by 7.5 billion schillings.
- Municipalities aim to reduce their deficits to 6.4 billion schillings from 11 billion so as to meet Maastricht criteria.
- Siegfried Sellitsch, chairman of Bank Austria, urges government to sell its 17 percent stake in the bank.
- Additional health security will be up to ten percent cheaper due to changes to tax laws which have to be done in accordance with EU law.
- Labour contract laws will raise the amount of work done illegally by some 10 billion schillings, study says.
- Veitsch-Radex's plant in northern China will start work this year.
- President Thomas Klestil, suffering from pneumonia, is recovering. Chancellor Franz Vranitzky will take over his duties for the next week.
- Energy prices went up 6.2 percent in August compared to the same month last year.
